case: Direct ClaimVerifier construction with self-generated reviewer keys and signed records
time_context: Reproduced during independent audit before the source-level factory-authority guard was added
workspace: Disposable OS temporary directory; removed in finally cleanup

policy_supplied_by_caller.roadmap: kind roadmap, links semantic and owner criteria, includes caller-generated traceability graph
policy_supplied_by_caller.semanticReview: caller-generated Ed25519 reviewer key with independent_reviewer / semantic_review role-purpose
policy_supplied_by_caller.ownerAcceptance: caller-generated Ed25519 reviewer key with product_owner / owner_acceptance role-purpose

records: Both records were signed by the same test process using caller-generated private keys and bound to the temporary roadmap hash; criterion observations were self-generated.
expected: Direct caller cannot establish trusted reviewer identity; overall non-PASS / reject unauthorized policy
classification: CRITICAL REVIEWER-TRUST ENTRY-POINT BYPASS reproduced. This is distinct from the B9.49 lexical roadmap-content bypass. The bypass was remediated by private canonical-policy authority enforcement and is covered by a permanent regression.

post_fix_regression.test: direct ClaimVerifier caller cannot inject roadmap reviewer trust keys

limitations: The source-pinned trust registry is empty; no production/owner key was configured.
The test proves the JavaScript API boundary for the tested path, not OS isolation or a general human-review quality guarantee.

The verifier source itself remains mutable workspace content outside the captured Git HEAD; source integrity must be established by an authorized review/version-control process before relying on it across trust domains.
